_status: Module 3, Lesson 3.1, 'VPNs: a private tunnel' (learner guide of 21 October 2026), including the Module 2 contractor case. Fictional office.
title: VPNs: a private tunnel

steps.title: Sol works from a café
steps.text: Without a VPN, office systems are not reachable from the internet at all, and anyone on the café Wi-Fi sees what is not encrypted.

steps.title: Through the VPN: an encrypted tunnel
steps.text: The VPN encrypts the connection between Sol's laptop and the office, after MFA. The person on the café Wi-Fi sees scrambled bytes; the firewall lets the tunnel reach only what Sol's role needs.

screen.title: What the café Wi-Fi sees
lines: (an encrypted tunnel: no names, no files)

steps.title: A contractor left two months ago
steps.text: His VPN password was stolen, and it is used at night from abroad.

ask.q: What two things should every VPN account have?
options: A long name and a photo
MFA, and closure on the person's last day
A shared password, so IT can help
ask.why: Every VPN account needs MFA, and the accounts of people who leave are closed on their last day.

steps.title: Password only: the attacker is in
steps.text: With a password alone, the tunnel opens for whoever has it.

steps.title: MFA, and the account closed on his last day
steps.text: MFA asks for a second proof the attacker does not have. Better still, the account was closed the day the contract ended.

verdict.text: MFA on every VPN account; close leavers' accounts on their last day.

tracks.label: Never open to the internet
tracks.desk: Use the VPN for office systems when away, and never share your VPN account.
tracks.it: MFA on VPN and admin accounts; no remote desktop open to the internet; decide split tunneling deliberately.

steps.title: Remote desktop sits behind the VPN
steps.text: Attackers scan the internet for remote desktop doors. At the RSSO there is none to find: remote desktop works only inside the VPN.

head: VPN fact
Why it matters
rows: Remote-access VPN connects one laptop; site-to-site connects two office networks
Both encrypt the connection between them
A stolen password alone does not open the tunnel
Leavers' accounts close on their last day
Module 2's contractor could still connect two months later
Split tunneling sends only office traffic through the VPN
Convenient, but home-network risks then sit next to office access: IT decides it deliberately
Remote desktop is never open directly to the internet
